source_text: Hoc igitur consignato, quid processum tuum consequatur attende. Prophetas et Patriarchas, omnesque sanctos Veteris Testamenti constat Baptismatis expertes fuisse, sed a Deo conditos propriis deinceps fulsisse virtutibus; sub diaboli ergo regno, contra testimonium legis, esse credentur aeternis suppliciis mancipandi; quia ex Adam omnes pronuntiantur a te in condemnationem creati.
pass_a_gloss: This therefore having been sealed, attend what follows your process. It stands that the Prophets and Patriarchs, and all the saints of the Old Testament were without Baptism, but founded by God thereafter shone by their own virtues; under the kingdom of the devil therefore, against the testimony of the law, they will be believed to be to be delivered to eternal punishments; because from Adam all are pronounced by you created into condemnation.

lemmas.lexica: LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: With this established, consider what follows from your course of argument. The prophets and patriarchs and all the saints of the Old Testament plainly did not receive baptism, yet were created by God and afterward shone with their own virtues. They must therefore, against the Law's testimony, be believed to belong to the devil's kingdom and be destined for eternal punishments, because you declare that all are created from Adam for condemnation (compare Romans 5:18).

choices.why: Keep the rite-name; Julian says praise of baptism is being used to smuggle natural evil.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
